title: English: Grammar and Punctuation (A2-B1)
source: Written for Kru, Nov 24 (Henry): 100 questions on grammar, punctuation and writing skills at A2-B1. American English.

questions.q: I have ___ apple in my bag.
questions.why: Apple starts with a vowel sound, so we use 'an'.
Teacher starts with a consonant sound, so we use 'a'.
There is only one sun, so we say 'the sun'.
Consonant + y: change y to i and add -es.
baby, babies: change y to i and add -es.
'Honest' starts with a vowel SOUND (the h is silent), so we use 'an'.
Many words ending in -fe change to -ves: knife, knives.
We usually say 'the' with musical instruments: play the guitar.
Honest starts with a vowel sound (the h is silent).
Egg starts with a vowel sound.

questions.q: We saw ___ elephant at the zoo.
questions.why: Elephant starts with a vowel sound.
Doctor starts with a consonant sound.
We both know which door, so we use "the".

questions.q: There are three ___ in the box.
Two ___ are playing in the park.
We use ___ hour to get to school.
questions.why: Hour starts with a vowel sound.
Umbrella starts with a vowel sound.
There is only one moon, so "the".

questions.q: I saw ___ movie yesterday. ___ movie was great.
questions.why: First mention: a. Second mention: the.
He, she and it take -s/-es in the present simple.
They + base verb in the present simple.
It is happening now, so we use the present continuous.
A habit: present simple. He + eats.
After 'does' we use the base verb: like.

questions.q: We ___ in the library now, so please be quiet.
I usually ___ coffee, but today I ___ tea.
questions.why: Usually = present simple. Today (now) = present continuous.
'Know' is a state verb, so we do not use it in the continuous.
Facts and science use the present simple.
"Look!" and "now" mean right now: present continuous.

questions.q: I ___ my homework at the moment.

questions.why: A job is a fact: present simple.

questions.q: The bus ___ at 8 o'clock every morning.
questions.why: A schedule is a fact: present simple.

questions.q: How often ___ you go to the movie theater?
She usually ___ jeans, but today she ___ a dress.
I ___ understand this word. Can you help?
questions.why: "Understand" is a state verb: use present simple.
"Having lunch" is an action in progress.

questions.q: My sister ___ a cake. It smells great!
We ___ not playing, we are studying.
What is the past tense of 'go'?
What is the past tense of 'play'?
She ___ to the park last Sunday.

questions.why: After 'did' we use the base verb.

questions.q: What is the past tense of 'buy'?

questions.why: Negative past simple: didn't + base verb.

questions.q: What is the past tense of 'study'?
questions.why: Consonant + y: change y to i and add -ed.

questions.q: I ___ him at the mall last night.
questions.why: After 'didn't' we use the base verb: see.

questions.q: While I ___ dinner, my phone rang.
questions.why: A longer action in the past (past continuous) is interrupted by a short one (past simple).

questions.q: I ___ to school by bike yesterday.
She ___ a letter to her friend.
We ___ pizza for dinner last night.
They ___ a big house two years ago.
I ___ my keys, so I couldn't open the door.
He ___ his arm when he fell.
They ___ to the party because they were tired.
An elephant is ___ than a dog.
questions.why: Short adjectives: add -er. Big doubles the g: bigger.

questions.q: Today is the ___ day of the year.
questions.why: The + adjective + -est for the highest degree.

questions.q: This book is ___ than that one.
He is the ___ student in the class.

questions.why: as + adjective + as shows two things are equal.

questions.q: Math is ___ than English for me.
questions.why: Difficult is long, so we use 'more' + adjective + than.

questions.q: The harder you study, the ___ your grades will be.
questions.why: The + comparative, the + comparative: the harder, the better.

questions.q: An elephant is ___ than a horse.
Tom is the ___ boy in our class.
This is the ___ cake in the shop.
Today is the ___ day of the year.
My bag is ___ than your bag.
The Mekong is ___ than the Chao Phraya.
She is the ___ singer in the school.
A cheetah is the ___ animal on land.
My phone is as ___ as yours.
Today is ___ than yesterday. It's lovely!
Who is the ___ in your family?
My house is ___ than his house.
This is the ___ street in town.

choices: She is more tall than me.

questions.q: The cat is ___ the box. (It is inside the box.)
She walked ___ the bridge to get to the other side.
questions.why: 'Across' means from one side to the other.
We say 'on the third floor' (on a level of a building).

questions.q: I go to school ___ Monday to Friday.

questions.why: "On" is for days and parts of a day on a date.

questions.q: The cat is hiding ___ the sofa.
The shop is ___ the bank and the school.
She is waiting ___ the bus stop.

questions.why: "Across" = from one side to the other.

questions.q: I'm looking ___ my phone. Have you seen it?
I sit ___ Ben and Mai in class.

questions.why: After 'can' we use the base verb and never add -s.
We ask about a thing or a name with 'What'.

questions.q: You ___ wear a seat belt. It's the law.
questions.why: 'Must' shows a strong rule or duty.

questions.q: You look sick. You ___ see a doctor.
You ___ bring a pen. We have extra pens.
questions.why: 'Don't have to' means it is not necessary.
After 'Would you mind' we use the -ing form.

questions.q: She ___ be at home. Her lights are on.
questions.why: 'Must' can also show that we are almost sure.

questions.q: You ___ wear a helmet on a motorcycle. It's the law.
You ___ see a doctor. You look ill.
I ___ swim when I was five.
She ___ come to the party, but she isn't sure.
You ___ park here. It's not allowed.
You ___ bring a pen. We have some.
___ is that girl? She's my cousin.
___ do you eat lunch? At noon.
___ is the library? Next to the school.
___ are you crying? I lost my phone.
___ do you go to school? By bus.
___ do you like, tea or coffee?
We ___ to wear a uniform at school.
___ you help me carry this bag?

questions.why: You cannot count water (one water, two waters).

questions.q: There is ___ milk in the fridge.
questions.why: Milk is uncountable, so we use 'some'.

questions.q: How ___ water do you drink a day?

questions.why: 'Information' is uncountable: no 'an' and no plural.

questions.q: There ___ a lot of people at the party.
I have ___ friends in this city, so I feel lonely.
There is only ___ sugar left, so we can't bake a cake.
questions.why: Sugar is uncountable; 'little' means almost none.

questions.q: How ___ apples are in the bag?
There isn't ___ milk in the fridge.
I have ___ friends in this school.

questions.why: You can't count "rice" one by one.
You can say one chair, two chairs.

questions.q: There are too ___ people on the bus.
Are there ___ eggs in the kitchen?

choices: There is a lot of sugar.
There are a lot of sugar.
There is a lot of sugars.

questions.q: There are ___ students in the room. It's almost empty.
He has ___ money. He can't buy a bike.

questions.why: Start a sentence and a name with a capital letter, and end with a period.
A question ends with a question mark.

questions.q: Which sentence uses commas correctly in a list?
choices: I like, pizza pasta and salad.
I, like pizza pasta, and salad.
I like pizza pasta, and, salad.
I like pizza, pasta, and salad.
questions.why: Put a comma between the things in a list.
Use 's to show that something belongs to one person.

questions.q: What is the short form of 'do not'?
questions.why: The apostrophe goes where the letter o is missing.
Days of the week start with a capital letter.
Use a comma before the quotation and quotation marks around the spoken words.

questions.q: Which sentence needs a question mark?
questions.why: 'Where is the library' asks a question.

choices: I wanted to go but, it was raining.
I wanted, to go but it was raining.
I wanted to go, but it was raining.
I wanted to go but it was, raining.
questions.why: Put a comma before 'but' when it joins two complete sentences.

questions.q: The two ___ bags are in the hall.
questions.why: For a plural noun ending in -s, we put the apostrophe after the s.

choices: I like pizza, pasta, and rice.
I like pizza pasta and rice.
I like, pizza pasta, and rice.
I like pizza, pasta and, rice.
questions.why: Commas separate items in a list.

choices: We visited chiang mai in january.
We visited Chiang Mai in January.
We visited Chiang mai in January.
we visited Chiang Mai in January.
questions.why: Names of places and months need capitals.
"Brother's" shows the bike belongs to him.
Use a comma inside the quote marks.

questions.q: Which word needs a capital letter?
questions.why: Days of the week start with capitals.

questions.q: Which word needs a capital letter?
questions.why: Names of countries start with capitals.

choices: Yesterday, I went to the park.
Yesterday I went, to the park.
Yesterday I, went to the park.
yesterday, I went to the park.
questions.why: A comma goes after an opening time word.

questions.q: Which sentence needs a question mark?
Which punctuation ends a command like "Stop"?

questions.why: Capital letter at the start of the quote.

choices: I have a cat a dog and a fish.
I have, a cat a dog and a fish.
I have a cat, a dog and, a fish.
I have a cat, a dog, and a fish.

questions.why: Question: capital at the start, "?" at the end; days have capitals.
'Their' shows that something belongs to them.
I before E, except after C: receive.

questions.q: I don't know ___ it will rain.
questions.why: 'Whether' means 'if'. 'Weather' is rain, sun and wind.
'Affect' is usually a verb. 'Effect' is usually a noun.
Definitely has the word 'finite' inside it.

questions.q: They put ___ bags on the table.
I can't ___ the board. Please move.
A ___ is a flying animal with fur.
I ___ my keys. Can you help me look?
The ___ is shining. It's a nice day.
I was tired, ___ I went to bed early.
I stayed home ___ it was raining.
Read: 'Tom gets up at 6:30. He eats breakfast at 7:00 and goes to school at 7:30.' What time does Tom eat breakfast?
questions.why: The text says he eats breakfast at 7:00.

questions.q: It's cloudy. I think it ___ rain.
We ___ visit my grandma this weekend. We bought the tickets.
questions.why: 'Be going to' is used for plans.

questions.q: Read: 'Mia has a small dog. The dog is brown and loves to run in the park.' What does the dog love?
questions.why: The text says the dog loves to run in the park.
'Never' is used with the present perfect (have + past participle).

questions.q: If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay home.
questions.why: In a first conditional, the 'if' part uses the present simple.

questions.q: I have known him ___ five years.
I'm tired, ___ I'm going to bed.
She is going to ___ a doctor.
Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
questions.why: A prediction from what we see.

questions.q: I think it ___ be sunny tomorrow.
I ___ help you with your bag.
I like cats ___ dogs. I like both!
He was sick, ___ he went to school.
She studied hard, ___ she passed the test.
First, mix the eggs. ___, add the flour.
I'm going to the shop. ___ do you want?
Tom has a dog. ___ name is Max.
"Mai is tall. She plays basketball." Who plays basketball?
"The shop opens at 9 and closes at 5." When does it close?
"Ben is ten. His sister is twelve." Who is older?
